issues.legal_issue: A compact disc containing a recorded conversation is a document for evidentiary purposes.
material_facts: The defence sought to introduce a compact disc containing a recorded conversation.
The compact disc was tendered in an ongoing criminal trial.
issues.conclusion: The compact disc is a document.
issues.legal_principle: Section 3 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 defines a document to include matter expressed or described on a substance for recording purposes. In R.M. Malkani v. State of Maharashtra and Ziyauddin Barhanuddin Bukhari v. Brijmohan Ramdass Mehra, the Court treated tape-recorded conversations as documents and described conditions relevant to their admissibility, including voice identification, accuracy and relevance.

predicates.recorded_conversation: A conversation was recorded and stored on a physical medium.
predicates.recording_stored_on_physical_medium: The recorded matter was preserved on a medium capable of being presented as evidence.

issues.definition: When a conversation is recorded and stored on a physical medium, that medium is treated as a document.

issues.legal_issue: An endorsement by counsel for the opposing side can satisfy the requirement to admit or deny the genuineness of a document.
material_facts: The defence filed a compact disc and sought to have it played so that the prosecution could admit or deny it.
The courts below rejected the defence application without allowing that process.
issues.conclusion: The opposing party’s counsel may endorse admission or denial on a document filed by the other side; the endorsement need not be obtained personally from the accused, complainant or witness.
issues.legal_principle: Section 294(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 requires the other side to be called upon to admit or deny the genuineness of a document filed in court. The Court held that counsel’s endorsement is sufficient compliance; for a document filed by the defence, the public prosecutor may make the endorsement. Section 294(3) permits an undisputed document to be read in evidence without formal proof, while a document not admitted must be proved by the party that filed it.

predicates.document_filed_in_criminal_proceeding: A party files a document before a court in a criminal proceeding.
predicates.opposing_side_counsel_endorses_admission: Counsel for the opposing side records whether the document’s genuineness is admitted or denied.

issues.definition: If a document is filed in a criminal proceeding and opposing counsel records an admission or denial, that endorsement satisfies the requirement for a response on genuineness.

issues.legal_issue: A court errs by refusing a defence application to have a compact disc played for admission or denial and forensic examination when the circumstances show a legitimate evidentiary purpose and no apparent effort to delay the trial.
material_facts: The accused sought to have a compact disc containing a conversation played so the prosecution could admit or deny it and to have it sent to a forensic laboratory.
The prosecution witnesses had been examined, the accused was in custody, and the defence evidence was still in progress.
The courts below rejected the application, and the Supreme Court found no apparent intention by the accused to prolong the trial.
issues.conclusion: The rejection of the application was erroneous; the application to have the compact disc played and processed for admission or denial and forensic examination was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 294 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 provides a procedure for admission or denial of documents and avoids unnecessary formal proof where genuineness is not disputed. The Court held that the defence had to be allowed to pursue that procedure for the compact disc, without expressing any view on the truth of the conversation or the ultimate merits of the case.

rule.if: criminal_trial and defense_offers_recording and seeks_playback_for_opposing_response and seeks_forensic_examination and accused_in_custody and prosecution_witnesses_examined and no_delay_tactic_apparent

predicates.criminal_trial: The proceeding is a criminal trial in which the accused is presenting a defence.
predicates.defense_offers_recording: The accused offers a recording as defence evidence.
predicates.seeks_playback_for_opposing_response: The accused asks for the recording to be played so the opposing side can admit or deny its genuineness.
predicates.seeks_forensic_examination: The accused asks for forensic examination of the recording.
predicates.accused_in_custody: The accused is in custody while the trial is proceeding.
predicates.prosecution_witnesses_examined: The prosecution has already examined its witnesses.
predicates.no_delay_tactic_apparent: The circumstances disclose no apparent intention by the accused to prolong the trial.

issues.definition: When the stated trial circumstances accompany a defence offer of a recording for response and forensic examination, the application to pursue those steps must be allowed.

issues.legal_issue: An accused is not entitled to bail solely on the ground of trial delay in the circumstances accompanying the allowance of the defence evidence application.
material_facts: The accused was in custody while the trial continued.
The prosecution witnesses had been examined, and the defence evidence was in progress.
The Court found no apparent intention by the accused to prolong the trial and allowed the application concerning the compact disc.
issues.conclusion: The accused was not entitled to seek bail on the ground of trial delay.
issues.legal_principle: The Court, having allowed the defence application in the circumstances of the case, expressly directed that the accused could not seek bail on the ground of trial delay. It did not state a broader rule for circumstances different from those before it.

rule.if: criminal_trial and accused_in_custody and prosecution_witnesses_examined and no_delay_tactic_apparent and defense_recording_application_allowed

predicates.criminal_trial: The proceeding is a criminal trial that has not concluded.
predicates.accused_in_custody: The accused is in custody while the trial is proceeding.
predicates.prosecution_witnesses_examined: The prosecution has already examined its witnesses.
predicates.no_delay_tactic_apparent: The circumstances disclose no apparent intention by the accused to prolong the trial.
predicates.defense_recording_application_allowed: The court allows the accused’s application concerning defence evidence.

issues.definition: When an accused is in custody in the stated trial circumstances and the defence evidence application is allowed, trial delay alone does not entitle the accused to bail.
